profile.name: Phrolova
profile.review:
Phrolova is a 5-star Havoc Rectifier DPS character best known for how meta-defining her release was. Phrolova is the gold standard of Whimpering Wastes; she’s almost defined by her presence in that specific endgame. Her kit focuses on everything ideal for WhiWa, on and off-field long-range attacks with quick in-and-out rotations, constant and evenly spread-out damage, and most importantly, the most impressive Crowd Control utility in the game in the form of her most important mechanic, Hecate, summoned via her Ultimate. Phrolova’s entire kit sums up to accessing that Ultimate as quickly as possible, and consequently making the most of it.

Music Theory

The text in this section is optional to read; it won’t really help you understand Phrolova’s kit any better, but we initially wrote it when making Phrolova’s review and thought it had some cool enough fun facts about the way Phrolova’s Forte is designed for you to read if you’re interested. So here you go:

Everything you need to keep track of in battle while playing Phrolova are a few key attacks you’ll access at certain points in her rotation, as well as her Forte gauge which resembles sheet music! So let’s analyze it and talk about music theory. Phrolova is playing a melody in treble clef, visible on her Forte gauge. This clef is used to sheet higher-pitched sounds (above the middle C on a piano). This clef is the most commonly used as it covers sheets for a wide variety of popular instruments including a lot of well-known string, wood and brass instruments such as, who could’ve known, the violin! That’s the thing Phrolova plays! But, she also uses a wand iconic of orchestra conductors to command Hecate, her partner who does attacks depending on the kind of notes she’s playing. She plays 3 quarter notes (also known as crotchets) in every bar. This is a time signature commonly used for Waltz Dancing! Kuro did really cool references to this character’s interests when designing her Forte, so props to them for that.

Regardless, in the Wuthering Waves world, this translates to about 1.5 to 3 seconds per Hecate attack (depending on whether it’s enhanced or not). Given our prior analysis on top of the fact she’s playing 6 notes total over a minimum of 9s (and a max of 18s!), we’re pretty sure she’s playing the slowest string of random notes known to mankind. Also, when you actually see Phrolova play the violin in-game, not only is she holding it super far away from her chin, which isn’t how you play the violin at all, but she’s playing the same notes over and over and somehow the background music sounds different. We honestly think she has superpowers if she’s supposed to be the one playing that.

Key Mechanics

Phrolova can actually play different melodies depending on how you operate her rotations in game. She acquires notes in a few manners, and has 3 different types of notes she can play.

  • String note: This is acquired by performing Basic Attack 3 or Enhanced Basic Attack and it has the effect of stagnating enemies;

  • Wind note: This is acquired by performing Skill or Enhanced Skill and it has the effect of grouping enemies;

  • Cadenza note: This is acquired twice per rotation by using any Intro or Echo Skill and it has the effects of both Wind and String notes at once.

We mentioned Phrolova has enhanced Basic Attacks and Skills. She accesses them by casting Basic Attack 3 or Skill. Her enhanced Basic Attack gives higher damage while her enhanced Skill is better at controlling multiple enemies, so what kind of note you choose with your Enhanced attacks should depend on what kind of encounter you’re facing, but in practice sticking to Enhanced Basics with most Phrolova compositions is fine - feel free to experiment with Enhanced Skills in Whimpering Wastes though. 

It’s also worth noting some notes simply won’t be changeable as they’ll be acquired by doing Basic 3’s and Skills which are the quickest way of accessing Phrolova’s Ultimate — which is your end goal, so you should always be rotating in that manner.

Speaking of her Ultimate, it has a strict 25s cooldown as it requires a Forte Heavy Attack to be cast before using it. It costs 0 Resonance Energy and Phrolova does not have any Resonance Energy of her own. It also summons Hecate to play the notes Phrolova accumulated in sequence, automatically as she is off-field. Phrolova’s Ultimate gives her a massive 120% off-field self-ATK buff, and in total Hecate’s damage represents about half of her total damage (the rest being dealt on-field). Most importantly, Hecate will attack with slower and weaker regular attacks unless other teammates cast unique Echo Skills, queuing up 1 faster & stronger enhanced Hecate attack per unique Echo Skill cast.

While Phrolova attacks with Hecate, she gains stacks of Aftersound each time, increasing her CRIT DMG by 2.5% up to a cap of 24 (she also gains 10 stacks when entering battle). Additionally, each stack of Aftersound increases the DMG Multiplier of her Forte Heavy Attack by 82.55% (additive). Each stack exceeding the cap of 24 will increase CRIT DMG by 1% (Not having this fully stacked right away is what makes her first rotation much weaker than the following ones). This extra CRIT DMG keeps ramping up as long as Phrolova isn’t out of combat, meaning she keeps getting stronger as the battle goes on. This can add up to temporary endgame buffs such as the one in Tower of Adversity 3 & 4, where she really starts dealing huge damage towards the end of the fight.

Lastly, Phrolova’s Outro amplifies Havoc DMG and Heavy Attack DMG by 20% and 25% respectively for 1 character, and queues up 2 extra Enhanced Hecate attacks to perform next.4

Rotation Concepts

By what we explained earlier, Phrolova’s goal is pretty clear: get your 6 notes up via Basic 3’s and Skills (3 total), cast your Forte Heavy Attack, finish all of that off with your Ultimate, Hecate does off-field attacks while you’re out. There’s however more to consider, such as how to access that quickly:

  • Basic 3 can be immediately cast after Intro. Without Intro available, Phrolova’s rotation requires more Basic Attacks, but it is best to cast her Ultimate first and have her start as the first member of your party in the rotation (to maximize uptime on off-field attacks and access her Enhanced Intro).

  • Switching her in from any other character while in combat immediately starts her at Basic 2, skipping Basic 1 entirely.

  • Her Intro has 2 variants, one being accessed without having cast her Ultimate, another with having cast it prior. The latter is significantly stronger than the former in terms of damage and acts as her Ultimate finisher and this instantly ends her Ultimate stance.

So essentially, the idea for her rotation is:

  • For most compositions, start your rotation with Phrolova by switching her in from any other character to cast Basic 2 and Basic 3. If an Intro is available, do Intro into Basic 3. In compositions with a general Support like Shorekeeper, Phrolova will still rotate last (provided you’re not in Whimpering Wastes and your Ultimates are available).

  • Do Enhanced attacks after every Basic 3 and Skill. After doing this 3 times, you’ll have generated enough notes to cast her Forte Heavy and unlock her Ultimate.

  • Finish the rotation off with your Ultimate then switch out, don’t forget to use your Echo during her rotation as well (typically best used after an Enhanced attack).

Meta Position & Conclusion

Phrolova is probably the most meta-relevant damage dealer from the 2.x version, Rinascita, and to this day retains use cases across basically all accounts that own her. She has the major downside of her Signature weapon being basically a requirement due to how much worse the permanent weapon options are for Rectifier damage dealers in general, but outside of that, Phrolova has practically no flaws, other than being part of a generation of damage dealers that’s simply weaker than the current standard.

Indeed, Phrolova being a late 2.x character simply does not compare to modern late 3.x characters like Hsin, Qingxiao or Yangyang: Xuanling in single-target damage output. This is her biggest and only real issue beyond her Signature weapon requirement. And that’s because Hecate is an insane Crowd Control utility, capable of keeping enemies stunned as long as Hecate casts enhanced attacks, or group them together essentially permanently in Whimpering Wastes. And that last part is particularly important.

Phrolova in Whimpering Wastes has been meta-defining since her release. As the Echo Skill engine kept getting expanded upon following her release with the likes of Qiuyuan, Sigrika and Lucilla, Phrolova has kept on acquiring new teammates that raised her ceiling in both gamemodes. While outshined by several options in Yangyang: Xuanling teams, her being a Havoc/Heavy Attack damage dealer also enables her to get carried as a Support in single-target-oriented teams; and all of this has good chances to remain true in the long term, though not guaranteed. Last but not least, she has 3 different avenues for teammates to buff her, being Havoc DMG, Echo Skill DMG & Echo Skill Casts, as well as Resonance Skill DMG. All three, added on top of generalist Supports, give her a huge variety of team options, and at the strictest minimum, Danjin+Buling will still allow her to get clearing scores in Endstate Matrix if literally all characters on your account are taken but them (even if that’s very difficult to make happen).

In conclusion, Phrolova is an excellent damage dealer to this day and the best-surviving DPS of the 2.x cast. Her notorious performance in Whimpering Wastes has led her to still retain a top spot in the meta of today, and although her numbers are weaker than the most modern DPS generations, that hasn’t stopped her from still seeing frequent use on all accounts, old and new, that chose her.
profile.pros:
• The premier Whimpering Wastes character since her release. Hecate is the best crowd control utility in the game, she deals fantastic damage relative to her field time, as it happens both on and off-field at regular intervals;

  • No Energy Regen requirements make building her easy - also, teams are very easy to form around her because Havoc, Skill, and Echo damage are 3 damage types that have a ton of options for buffers;

  • Her Outro buff paired with good personal damage relative to her rotation time makes her a good secondary for some Havoc/Heavy ATK damage dealers (particularly considering her rotation time) - literally will never be stranded for teammates.
profile.cons:
• Really bad permanent weapon options; Signature is really strongly recommended to compete;

  • Lacks damage numbers nowadays to be a sufficient Hypercarry DPS for Tower of Adversity, so she will have trouble dealing with that game mode without at least one of good gameplay, good investment, or good teammates surrounding her;

  • The pioneer of kits the size of the Empire State Building… RIP my easily read & understood characters.

profile.rotations:
Rotation & How to Play

Phrolova’s rotation goal is to build up 6 notes as quickly as possible through her Basic Attacks and Skills in order to cast her Heavy: Scarlet Coda to access her Ultimate and switch out. Below are the most optimal ways to achieve this goal.

Echo Timing

Use Nightmare: Hecate after her second Enhanced Attack (as there’s nothing other than a Dash to cancel it with otherwise). This is directly written into her rotations; in niche situations/team compositions, it’s also possible to Swap Cancel it when cast.

Opener Rotation

In teams without a generalist Support like Shorekeeper, Phrolova is always best used by doing her rotation first (particularly important in Whimpering Wastes’ First Half where no Resonance Energy is granted, as her Ultimate doesn’t require any to cast). She may rotate like so:

  • Switch in from any other character in combat

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3 (Interrupt on first hit via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Skill)

  • Skill

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Echo)

  • Echo

  • Basic 1

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3 (Interrupt on first hit via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Heavy)

  • Heavy: Scarlet Coda (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Outro

At S1 and higher, Phrolova can and should skip her final Basic 123 → Dash → Forte Basic combo and cast Heavy: Scarlet Coda much quicker, since she generates 2 extra Notes through the S1. This allows for faster Openers (Loops remain unchanged, even in the first rotation, in order to consistently meet Support character cooldowns).

Optionally, if you want to privilege Forte Skills instead of Forte Basics, you can remove any Dash Cancels and cancel the animation of the Forte Skill when the portal opens in the animation instead (about half a second into the animation) to preserve its damage.

Loop Rotation

Easiest rotation to perform, doable once any Intro is available (should be prioritized when Phrolova’s Intro: Suite of Immortality is accessible as it deals a lot of damage on cast).

  • Intro: Suite of Immortality

  • Basic 3 (Interrupt on first hit via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Skill)

  • Skill

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Echo)

  • Echo

  • Basic 1

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3 (Interrupt on first hit via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Heavy)

  • Heavy: Scarlet Coda (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Outro

Optionally, if you want to privilege Forte Skills instead of Forte Basics, you can remove any Dash Cancels and cancel the animation of the Forte Skill when the portal opens in the animation instead (about half a second into the animation) to preserve its damage.

4 Forte Rotation

Rotation extension for Phrolova in teams that rotate in less than 25 seconds (her Ultimate’s cooldown). Should only be used on Loop Rotations as the Opener should be executed as quickly as possible. Anything over 4 Forte will result in any active Outro buffs on Phrolova expiring on the last hit of her Scarlet Coda though, which you really don’t want to happen.

  • Intro: Suite of Immortality

  • Basic 3 (Interrupt on first hit via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Skill)

  • Skill

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Echo)

  • Echo

  • Basic 1

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3 (Interrupt on cast via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Dash)

  • Dash

  • Basic 1

  • Basic 2

  • Basic 3 (Interrupt on cast via Dash)

  • Basic: Movement of Fate and Finality (Cancel animation on cast via Dash)

  • Heavy: Scarlet Coda (Cancel animation endlag via Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Outro

As usual, the same concept can be used with Forte Skills, though this tends to not be recommended as Phrolova’s rotation starts getting really long at that point (Forte Basics can be cancelled quicker than Forte Skills, leading to faster rotations by about 0.2s per Forte).

skills.name: Movement of Life and Death
skills.description:
Basic Attack

Perform up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Havoc DMG.

When performing Basic Attack Stage 3, enter Reincarnate state.

Heavy Attack

Consume STA to attack the target, dealing Havoc DMG.

Press Normal Attack shortly after casting this skill to cast Basic Attack Stage 2.

Scarlet Coda

Phrolova enters the Compose state every 25s.

When the following 3 conditions are met, Heavy Attack is replaced with Scarlet Coda.

  • Has 6 Volatile Notes.

  • In the Compose state.

  • Not in the Resolving Chord state.

Scarlet Coda: Consume STA to deal Havoc DMG, Stagnating and pulling in nearby targets. This instance of damage is considered Resonance Skill DMG.

Each stack of Aftersound additionally increases the DMG Multiplier of this instance of damage.

Casting this skill is considered as casting Echo Skill.

Casting this skill sends Compose state into cooldown and activates the Resolving Chord state.

Mid-air Attack

Consume STA to perform a Plunging Attack, dealing Havoc DMG.

Dodge Counter

Press Normal Attack after a successful Dodge to attack the target, dealing Havoc DMG.

Press Normal Attack shortly after casting this skill to cast Basic Attack Stage 3.

skills.name: Whispers in a Fleeting Dream
skills.description:
Attack the target and deal Havoc DMG.

Casting this skill sends Phrolova into Reincarnate.

skills.name: Waltz of Forsaken Depths
skills.description:
Waltz of Forsaken Depths

Phrolova's max Resonance Energy is 0. Waltz of Forsaken Depths does not consume Resonance Energy.

When in the Resolving Chord state, Waltz of Forsaken Depths becomes available.

Casting this skill ends the Resolving Chord state, and Phrolova enters the Maestro state for 24s.

Maestro

Gain 120% ATK increase.

Phrolova floats in the air and commands Hecate to fight. Hecate will share Phrolova's stats and statuses, and damage dealt by Hecate will be considered coming from Phrolova. Hecate's attacks will not remove the target's Hazy Dream state.

During this period, Phrolova plays the Volatile Notes in turn. Each Volatile Note holds for 4s.

If Phrolova is the active Resonator on the field, she can give the following cues to Hecate. Any damage taken by Hecate in this state affects Phrolova as well.

  • Cue - Basic Attack: Press Normal Attack to command Hecate to cast Basic Attack - Hecate. When Phrolova is the active Resonator on the field, for every 2 times Hecate casts Basic Attack - Hecate, the next Basic Attack - Hecate is replaced with Enhanced Attack - Hecate.

  • Cue - Dodge: Press Dodge to command Hecate to dodge an attack. Hecate takes no damage from a hit successfully Dodged.

  • Cue - Reset: Press Jump to reset Hecate's position.

  • Cue - Curtain Call: Press Resonance Liberation to command Hecate to cast Curtain Call and end the Maestro state.

When Phrolova is not the active Resonator, Hecate takes no damage and automatically casts Basic Attack - Hecate to attack the target. When Resonators in the team cast Echo Skill, Hecate casts Enhanced Attack - Hecate to attack the target. This effect can be triggered up to 10 times in total during Phrolova's Maestro state. Echoes of the same name can trigger this effect 1 times.

Switching back to Phrolova ends Maestro state.

Ending Maestro state removes all Volatile Notes.

Basic Attack - Hecate

Perform up to 2 consecutive attacks, dealing Havoc DMG (considered Echo Skill DMG).

Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Strings

When Phrolova plays Volatile Note - Strings, Hecate casts Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Strings when casting Enhanced Attack - Hecate, dealing Havoc DMG and Stagnating the targets (considered Echo Skill DMG).

Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Winds

When Phrolova plays Volatile Note - Winds, Hecate casts Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Winds when casting Enhanced Attack - Hecate, dealing Havoc DMG, pulling the targets in (considered Echo Skill DMG).

Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Cadenza

When Phrolova plays Volatile Note - Cadenza, Hecate casts Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Cadenza when casting Enhanced Attack - Hecate, dealing Havoc DMG, Stagnating and pulling the targets in (considered Echo Skill DMG).

Curtain Call

Curtain Call can be cast via the following 5 ways, Stagnating the targets and dealing Havoc DMG.

  • When Phrolova is the active Resonator on the field, end the Maestro state.

  • When Phrolova is in the Maestro state, switch to Phrolova without casting Intro Skill.

  • When Phrolova is not the active Resonator and the Maestro state ends, switch to Phrolova without casting Intro Skill.

  • When Phrolova is in the Maestro state, press Resonance Liberation.

  • When Phrolova is in the Resolving Chord state, hold Resonance Liberation.

When in Resolving Chord state, casting Curtain Call removes all Volatile Notes and ends the Resolving Chord state.

multipliers.Name: Waltz of Forsaken Depths Concerto Regen

skills.name: Rhapsody of a New World
skills.description:
Basic Attack - Movement of Fate and Finality

When in Reincarnate, press Normal Attack on the ground to cast Movement of Fate and Finality, which Stagnates the target, dealing Havoc DMG (considered Resonance Skill DMG) and ending Reincarnate afterward.

Resonance Skill - Murmurs in a Haunting Dream

When in Reincarnate, press Resonance Skill on the ground to cast Murmurs in a Haunting Dream, dealing Havoc DMG (considered Resonance Skill DMG) and ending Reincarnate afterward.

Aftersound

Phrolova can hold up to 24 stacks of Aftersound.

When Phrolova is not the active Resonator, casting Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Strings, Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Winds, and Enhanced Attack - Hecate: Cadenza grants 1 stacks of Aftersound.

When Phrolova is out of combat, all stacks of Aftersound are removed every 30s.

Volatile Note

Phrolova can hold up to 6 Volatile Notes. When Volatile Notes reach the max number, gaining new Volatile Notes moves all Volatile Notes one slot to the left, and the leftmost Volatile Note - Strings or Volatile Note - Winds will be removed.

Hitting a target with Basic Attack Stage 3 or Movement of Fate and Finality grants 1 Volatile Note - Strings.

Hitting a target with Resonance Skill Whispers in a Fleeting Dream or Resonance Skill Murmurs in a Haunting Dream grants 1 Volatile Note - Winds.

When Inherent Skill - Accidental is activated, casting Suite of Quietus, Suite of Immortality, or Echo Skill grants 1 Volatile Note - Cadenza.

Phrolova cannot obtain Volatile Notes during Resolving Chord.

Suite of Immortality

skills.name: Unfinished Piece

The incoming Resonator gains 20% Havoc DMG Amplification and 25% Heavy Attack DMG Amplification for 14s or until they are switched out.

If Phrolova is in Maestro state when she casts this skill, Hecate additionally casts Enhanced Attack - Hecate 2 times when Phrolova is switched off the field while in the same Maestro state duration.

If Phrolova is not the active Resonator during the Maestro state, targets take 40% more DMG from Hecate and Phrolova. If Phrolova is the active Resonator during the Maestro state, gain 60% Havoc DMG Bonus.

profile.calculationsNotes:
Important! Phrolova's rotation time is calculated assuming that all of her off-field attacks are performed but not counted in her rotation time, which is something that we did for all off-field attackers as well (such as Zhezhi, or Cantarella for example). This significantly skews Phrolova's DPS number compared to on-field attackers and we'll once again remind you to not consider this number for meta assessment as per our disclaimers written above.

All calculations assume the following:

  • Hecate is already spawned in;
  • Phrolova has her Enhanced Intro available (neither of these things are possible on the first rotation).

Aftersound Stacks are calculated in a specific manner: We did an average over 4 rotations of the amount of Aftersound stacks that can be accumulated by Phrolova and 2 Echo Skills from any teammates (no other buffs provided, opener with 10 stacks included). This number of stacks and Phrolova's overall damage can be boosted by Cantarella's presence on the team, as well as a higher number of rotations and Echoes with more than one use charge such as Nightmare: Crownless - we settled on this average over 4 rotations to reflect Phrolova's performance in the maximum amount of time to full clear Tower of Adversity / Whimpering Wastes in the widest variety of teams possible. For Enhanced Hecate attacks, the same rules apply; only 2 Echo casts from other teammates are considered, but Phrolova's damage can be enhanced by Cantarella as well as Echoes with multiple uses.

Sequence comments:

  • S2 - This Sequence's performance is impacted by the way we chose to calculate Aftersound stacks, and its value may be increased or decreased depending on the amount of rotations Phrolova executes over the course of a battle (for this specific Sequence, more rotations = lower value).
  • S3 - Due to the fact that Phrolova's opening rotation doesn't include Hecate, the value this sequence provides can vary. In longer fights with more rotations that have Hecate active, this sequence will perform better, on the contrary the less rotations are performed, the less Hecate is present over the fight, the lower this sequence's value is. Additionally, the more amplification you already have on Phrolova, the less impact the amplification this sequence will have (these calculations consider Phrolova's perfromance in a vacuum, adding more amplification will reduce it's value compared to what is displayed).
  • S6 - Similar to S3, this sequence will reduce in value the less rotations Hecate is active for, meaning it'll be stronger in longer fights but weaker in shorter fights. The inverse would normally apply due to how Aftersound stack calculations are handled, but since S2 is already contributing heavily to this goal, this sequence is overall more impactful over longer fights.

And since Phrolova is very reliant on her signature weapon, we have prepared her sequences calculations too:

Phrolova with S1 Lethean Elegy

  • S6 — 2,763,617 DMG (219,631 DPS) (287.4%)
  • S5 — 1,817,187 DMG (144,416 DPS) (188.9%)

weapons.Comment: Phrolova's Signature is her best weapon by a huge margin. The passive alone give ATK, Skill DMG Bonus, Echo Skill DMG Amplification AND DEF Ignore. Pair that with its good base stats, this weapon is her best option bar none.

Stringmaster is able to give Phrolova good base ATK but most importantly massive amounts of CRIT Rate, ATK% and DMG Bonus, with an even bigger ATK boost off-field which matches her playstyle. Unfortunately for Phrolova, she buffs her ATK by massive amounts already which dilutes this buff, so her Signature is still recommended over this.

Phrolova is able to fully take advantage of this weapon's Havoc RES Shred effect when casting her Forte Heavy Attack, as it is also counted as an Echo Skill on top of her own Echo Skill cast. Unfortunately for Phrolova, this means it only buffs a small portion of her rotation as her Forte Heavy Attack is one of the last abilities she does before switching out, and she doesn't benefit that much from the Basic Attack DMG part of this weapon's passive.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat stick for Phrolova who draws little benefit from this weapon's Basic ATK DMG-increasing effect.
Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat stick for Phrolova who draws little benefit from this weapon's Spectro Frazzle-related effects.

The best permanent weapon option available for Phrolova, which unfortunately doesn't provide much for her beyond ATK% and Basic ATK DMG Bonus, both of which she doesn't draw much benefit from, further widening the gap between standard and Signature. Generally nowadays, we recommend just going for Phrolova's Signature.

Best 4-star weapon, this Battle Pass exclusive gives good Base ATK to Phrolova while providing additional CRIT Rate. Additionally, its effect which increases ATK when casting Ultimate is good to buff Phrolova's off-field attacks, but unfortunately this buff will get diluted a lot by her 120% self-ATK buff when casting Ultimate which negates a lot of its benefits.
This Battle Pass exclusive grants Phrolova with a nice CRIT DMG boost as well as extra ATK and Basic DMG when casting Skill. One of her better 4-star choices while not being ideal.

One of the best 4-star weapons for Phrolova which simply gives Base ATK and ATK% with a further boost to ATK% when casting Resonance Skill, as its flat Energy boost is wasted on her. Falls behind the above weapon options due to a lack of good stats.

Best fully F2P-accessible option, selectable for free at the start of the game or obtained through gacha. Gives a lot of ATK% via its stats and its passive activated upon Intro, but doesn't provide anything else.

echoes.Comment: Best Echo set for Phrolova as it permanently gives her 20% CRIT Rate and 35% Echo Skill DMG Bonus, providing big boosts to the majority of her rotation. Additionally, this is a 3-piece set, meaning it can be combined with a 2-piece set effect of your choice. Only used on Phrolova as its effects can only be activated when the equipped character has 0 Resonance Energy, something only Phrolova can upkeep permanently. This set is best combined with your choice of:
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: A Transform Echo that is quick to cast but extends Phrolova's rotation by one second approximately, which is a worthy trade-off as it provides a 12% Havoc and 20% Echo Skill DMG Bonus when placed in the main slot.

skillPriority.Comments: Skill and Intro can be skipped when levelling to save on resources at a minimal damage loss.

teams.Name: Team #1: Best Team
teams.Comments: Lucilla is only best in the 2nd slot with Qiuyuan as the 3rd, and is not recommended with Shorekeeper. In general, unless with Qiuyuan she pivots to the 3rd slot with another character Outro buffing Phrolova.

teams.Name: Team #2: Alternative Teams
teams.Comments: Only use Sigrika alongside Qiuyuan. Danjin + Roccia is also a possible pairing where Roccia moves to the third slot.

teams.Name: Team #3: Dual DPS
teams.Comments: Suisui and Chisa are only best with Yangyang: Xuanling - else, prioritize Shorekeeper.

teams.Name: Team #4: Phoebe Dual DPS
teams.Comments: Similar concept to Jiyan, with Spectro Rover acting as the Support. One of Phoebe's best teams assuming Phrolova has her Signature weapon.

synergies.Comment: Phrolova's best 2nd slot partners are listed here, each work well for different reasons: Lucilla can increase the whole party's Echo DMG and do high personal damage on her own, particularly useful with Qiuyuan or as a 3rd slot teammate without him. Cantarella works on her own as she also sports multiple Echo Skill casts and a strong Outro buff to increase Phrolova's on-field damage. Sigrika works well with Qiuyuan or Lucilla to fully activate her kit as a dual DPS option, and lastly Lynae does too as a general buffer for Phrolova and her whole team without extra Echo Skill casts.

These are all of the best 3rd slot teammates for Phrolova in order of who's strongest. Danjin and Roccia can also be used in the second slot provided Cantarella isn't available. They are all fantastic recipients of Phrolova's Outro as they deal a good chunk of Heavy Attack damage. Qiuyuan has multiple Echo Skill casts and buffs team-wide Echo Skill DMG which makes him the best choice. Roccia is also fantastic as she fully benefits from Phrolova's Outro and has an extra Echo Skill cast with her Magic Box, and Danjin is the last option but still very strong due to having a good Outro, a short rotation, and party-wide buffing via her S6.

Yangyang: Xuanling, Galbrena, Jiyan and Phoebe are Heavy Attack damage dealers and Phrolova is a Heavy Attack damage amplifier (in the case of Yangyang, she also amplifies her Havoc DMG). While Phrolova would traditionally not be relegated to the role of a buffer for a DPS, and indeed she is built like a DPS no matter what, Phrolova has the ability to buff the damage of these characters while dealing her own big amounts of damage off-field,  and also provide the best Crowd Control utility in the game in the form of Hecate, making these pairings quite strong, particularly with Yangyang: Xuanling who takes full advantage of her Outro!

These are all of Phrolova's 3rd slot teammate options. Shorekeeper is the best for all ATK and CRIT-scaling DPS due to her super high buffs for a short rotation time. Buling and Verina still do present themselves as good F2P alternatives because Buling trades team-wide ATK buffs for Skill DMG buffs to Phrolova and more personal damage for slightly higher rotation times, while Verina retains a good amount of buffs for one of the shortest rotation times in the game. Especially at S6, Buling can hence even be stronger than Verina in most Phrolova teams.
